finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the unsanitized query parameter f is joined to /srv/files, and filepath.Join cleans '..' segments so they escape the root. Any unauthenticated client can read arbitrary files the process can access.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter 'f' on GET /dl (files.go:12), attacker-controlled
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, response body written at files.go:18

trace.note: name := r.URL.Query().Get("f") — raw user input, e.g. ../../etc/passwd
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to /etc/passwd, with no prefix check against root
file contents returned to the client

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, no filepath.Base, no Clean-and-prefix check, no os.Root or fs.FS confinement. Only error handling (404 on read failure). Compare avatar(), which uses filepath.Base; download() lacks this.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 pass the raw query parameter f into filepath.Join(root, name) with no Base, prefix check or auth (the route is registered bare at files.go:32), so "../../etc/passwd" cleans to /etc/passwd and files.go:18 writes it to the response.
